samples.question: Exactly one ribbon in this picture is orange; every other ribbon is pale green-gray. The orange ribbon is a single unbranching chain of six equal square panels joined edge to edge by narrower necks, so it has exactly two ends and every other panel has exactly two neighbours along the ribbon. A solid black triangle outside one end panel points at the end where the ribbon starts. Each panel carries a 5 by 5 field of small dark square dots and empty cells, but that field is printed in the ribbon's own travel frame, not in the frame of the page: within a panel, a row runs in the direction the ribbon leaves that panel toward the next panel along the chain, from the panel's first column to its fifth, and the rows are numbered in the quarter-turn clockwise from that direction. The final panel uses the direction by which the ribbon arrived at it. Carry out this operation: read every panel's 5 by 5 field in that panel's own travel frame, lay all six fields on top of one another so that cell (row, column) meets cell (row, column), and keep exactly the cells that carry a dot in every one of the six panels. Exactly 9 of the 25 cells survive. The surviving cells form one symbol on the 5 by 5 grid: 'plus' is the full centre row together with the full centre column, 'ex' is the two full diagonals, 'tee' is the full top row together with the centre column below it, and 'ell' is the full left column together with the full bottom row. No single panel shows the symbol, the ribbon's path across the page is not the symbol, the pale ribbons are decoration, and stacking the panels in page orientation instead of each panel's own travel frame does not give the symbol. Which symbol do the surviving cells form? Answer with exactly one of: ell, ex, plus, tee.
